messages:
A Johnson: Heads-up — we need a tight contract from runtime/infra so Console can render per-customer quota and noisy-neighbor panels. Who owns the metric keys?
Maya Patel: +1. We need org-scoped metrics we can query without expensive joins. prefer labels: org_id, route, model_variant.
Rafael Cruz: runtime already emits per-request labels but they're coarse. We can add `org_id` label, but cost/series explosion is a concern.
Claire Li: can we limit cardinality by tagging only customer routes that have >X qps or reserved capacity?
Sumeet Rao: yep — proposal: default aggregation at org_id truncated bucket (hash16) + opt-in full org_id for Dedicated. reduces series while still enabling isolation.
A Johnson: That sounds reasonable. Console needs these specific metrics for dashboards: token_rate_per_org, request_concurrency_per_org, gpu_utilization_per_org, kv_cache_hit_rate_per_org.
Rafael Cruz: we can emit those. kv cache hit rate will be sampled from the runtime node exposing `kv_hits_total{org_id=...}` and `kv_requests_total{org_id=...}`.
Liu (devex): For Console UX — can we get a stable route_id and model_variant label so customers see which model variant caused spikes? Also need timestamped rollup windows (1m/5m/1h).
Sumeet Rao: yes, add `route_id` and `model_variant` labels. rollups are produced by the metrics pipeline, not runtime — we can add raw counters from runtime and let pipeline handle rollups.
Hannah (PM): Quick product ask: dashboards should expose noisy-neighbor early-warning signals (sustained high token_rate per_org, rising 95p latency, drop in kv_cache_hit_rate). Need a simple rule builder in Console to toggle alerts.
A Johnson: Agree. For alerting we'll need stable metric names and a recommended rule set. Suggested baseline rules:
```
- token_rate_per_org > 200k tokens/min sustained 5m
- request_concurrency_per_org > 80% of reserved_capacity sustained 2m
- gpu_utilization_per_org > 90% with increased tail latency
```
Maya Patel: telemetry pipeline note: we need an `ingest_source` label (hosted/dedicated/private) so Console respects privacy guards for Private deployments.
Rafael Cruz: private deployments won't have org_id exported off-box by default; we'll emit local-only metrics and a metadata manifest the console can read via the private control plane.
Claire Li: privacy ok. Also want a summary index metric `org_noise_index{org_id}` computed in pipeline combining z-scored token_rate, cpu_spike_count, kv_miss_ratio — fine to iterate.
Liu (devex): can we get example PromQL snippets for the Console team? e.g.:
```
sum by (org_id) (rate(tokens_generated_total[1m]))
sum by (org_id) (avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[5m]))
```
Sumeet Rao: will add to runtime spec. Also adding a `quota_bucket` label for requests hitting quota boundaries so we can visualize throttles.
Hannah (PM): timeline? we need something for the next UX sprint in 3 weeks. Minimal viable: emit org_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_generated_total, requests_total, kv_hits_total, kv_requests_total, gpu_utilization_percent.
Rafael Cruz: engineering estimate: 2 weeks to add labels + counters in runtime + 3 days to validate in staging metrics cluster.
Maya Patel: pipeline changes (rollups + noise_index) another 2 weeks. Console can start building with raw counters and fallback to aggregate views.
A Johnson: action items:
- Rafael: PR for runtime metric labels + counters (due in 2w)
- Sumeet: define promos/limits for cardinality and `hash16` plan (this week)
- Liu: prototype Console queries/widgets using example PromQL (start now)
- Hannah: draft alert rule recommendations and share with SRE/security for review (48h)
infra-bot: Deployment check: runtime can ship metric changes only in feature flag gated rollout.
Rafael Cruz: noted. will gate with `org_metrics_v2` flag and run a canary on staging.
Claire Li: one more ask — include `trace_id` on sampled error logs so Console can deep-link to traces when noisy neighbor is detected.
Sumeet Rao: we'll add `trace_id` to sampled error spans, yes.
A Johnson: cool. I'll follow up with a short spec doc summarizing labels, metric names, and the privacy constraints. Thanks all :thumbsup:
